concepts.description: The analyzer accepts files, directories, or repositories and combines pattern matching, AST analysis, and data-flow analysis.
All listed languages receive full syntax, security, and complexity analysis; type depth remains full, assisted, or partial according to the source matrix.
Style analysis covers formatting, naming, unused symbols, dead code, line length, and missing documentation.
Bug analysis covers null dereferences, type mismatches, bounds errors, resource leaks, races, and unreachable paths.
Security analysis covers injection and XSS, authentication weaknesses, secret exposure, XXE, missing authorization, misconfiguration, and vulnerable dependencies.
Complexity reporting includes cyclomatic, cognitive, Halstead, physical and logical LOC, and inheritance depth.
Dependency analysis covers outdated, vulnerable, unused, circular, and license-incompatible dependencies.
Quick is essential-only, standard is balanced, strict enables all rules, and security focuses on vulnerabilities.
Reports can be emitted to console, JSON, HTML, or GitHub-compatible SARIF.
Per-language enablement, rules, ignores, and JavaScript extension selection remain configurable.
Dependency scanning, secret checks, and OWASP checks remain independently configurable.
Cyclomatic, cognitive, line-length, and function-length limits retain their individual thresholds.
Errors are merge-blocking, warnings require review, and info or hint findings are optional.
The canonical console sample retains locations, per-finding severities and rule classes, and the aggregate summary.
The pre-commit hook analyzes staged changes and blocks at error severity.
GitHub Actions checks out code, produces SARIF, and uploads the same results file through CodeQL.
VS Code uses an extension, IntelliJ uses an external tool, and Vim or Neovim uses ALE or coc.nvim.
The API-key custom rule matches hardcoded assignments and emits an error for Python and JavaScript.
The fetch custom rule detects calls without catch handling and emits a warning for JavaScript and TypeScript.
Large-codebase analysis remains incremental, parallel, cached, and streaming.
Small, medium, and large LOC bands retain their separate target completion times.
Binary files are excluded from analysis.
Generated code may create false positives.
Feature support and accuracy vary by language, and custom frameworks may require custom rules.
Begin with standard, prioritize errors, integrate early, customize exceptions, and periodically run full analysis.
Historical trend analysis remains part of the analyzer capability.
Rule, security, custom-rule, and CI/CD references retain their respective guide roles.
